attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis in his newsletter. He quotes Oracle's tweet but rejects it in his own words.

semantics.note: Faithfully captures the two parts: power for only two buildings, and not on schedule, as of late April 2026.

contract.note: The contract fairly asks for a missed milestone that was due by April and treats the mid-2026 completion target as not yet failed. The speaker named no schedule, so the result depends on which baseline applies.

evidence.note: Oracle's dated post says 200MW operational. Per e2, that is roughly two buildings' worth, which supports the capacity part. Its 'on schedule' line is a company self-claim.
Original plan: two buildings at 200+MW energized in H1 2025, and six more by mid-2026. That target was still in the future in April 2026.
Crusoe says the first two buildings were energized within about a year. This weakens any claim that the first phase slipped, but says nothing on later milestones.

reviews.rationale: Two buildings' worth of capacity (about 200MW) is supported. The packet shows no milestone due by April 22–28 that was missed. The mid-2026 completion target had not yet passed, and phase one seems roughly on time. Oracle's own 'on schedule' claim is a company statement. The delay allegation, which is the core of the claim, is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own hypothetical model, in his own words.

semantics.note: Correctly framed as the output of the author's model. The 100% utilization and loan-term conditions are kept.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats two questions separately: is the arithmetic right, and is 'gross margin' the right label. The level-payment reading is the ordinary one.

evidence.note: The speaker's own inputs. Attached evaluator arithmetic reproduces 5.19% from the rounded totals.
The speaker's inputs. Evaluator math gives $54.1M a month and about $649.6M a year. It reaches about −40% only by subtracting both depreciation and full principal repayment.
SEC guide: repaying a loan is a financing cash flow, not a profit-and-loss expense. Accounting background only.

reviews.rationale: The arithmetic checks out under the stated assumptions: 5.19% margin, $54.1M a month, about $649M a year, and roughly −40%. But the −40% 'gross margin' subtracts depreciation on the same assets the loan principal pays for. That mixes an expense with financing cash flows, which meets the contract's contradiction condition for the label. Without depreciation, the cash residual is about +8.9%. The numbers hold; the −40% gross-margin description does not.

attribution.note: Zitron states the figures as fact in his own words. They reportedly come from Sightline, but he endorses them.

semantics.note: Keeps the 114GW group due by end-2028 and the 15.2GW under-construction share.

contract.note: Using an April 2026 snapshot with both figures drawn from the same set of projects is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: A March 2026 Sightline figure on the 2026 group only (16GW due, 5GW real). It covers a different group and date, so it cannot check the 114/15.2GW figures.

reviews.rationale: No independent record in the packet reproduces 114GW due through 2028 and 15.2GW under construction for the same set of projects. The only tracker item covers a different group and an earlier date, so the claim can be neither confirmed nor refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, in a polemical passage.

semantics.note: A passing, hyperbolic clause in a polemic about people who crave being 'first'. 'Repeating other actions' is undefined. The drafter's 'cannot do genuinely new things' firms up a loose aside into a technical impossibility claim.

contract.note: The contract counts an LLM paired with an external evaluator and evolutionary search as 'LLMs'. That stretches the speaker's statement about LLMs' own mechanism. It also equates 'something new' with verified scientific novelty, a reading the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: A peer-reviewed FunSearch paper reporting new cap-set constructions, but from an LLM-plus-evaluator search system. It does not directly test the vague restriction on LLMs themselves.

reviews.rationale: The clause is rhetorical, and its key term ('repeating other actions') has no testable definition. Scoring it requires an interpretation the speaker never gave, namely counting systems with external evaluators as LLMs. FunSearch is relevant background but cannot fairly settle a claim this vague.
